description: [allAfrica] The first Youth Olympic Games held on the African continent, the Dakar 2026 YOG, concluded on November 13th with a record praised by leaders of the Olympic movement. Beyond the organizational success and popular enthusiasm, Senegal and its partners now face a major challenge: transforming this historic first into an engine of sporting, economic, and social development. Youth training, job creation, infrastructure development, and the emergence of new talent are the main priorities for the post-Games
title: Africa: Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games - After The Historic Achievement, The Challenge of a Lasting Legacy for Africa

description: [Bird Story Agency] Kenya's all-women coaching staff turned a squad full of wingers into a team that could come from behind to win Olympic gold. One concerned a demand to triple adaptation finance, the other related to trade-related climate measures like carbon border taxes and the last one was about financing arrangements under the Green Climate Fund (GCF), a climate fund established under the UNFCCC to

description: [The Conversation Africa] Black rhinos are notoriously aggressive, not just to humans, but also to their fellow black rhinos. Aggression is so prevalent that injuries sustained after fighting with another black rhino are a common cause of death. Because of this aggression and their solitary nature, black rhino social behaviour has been largely unexplored. Yet it may be key to conservation of this critically endangered African icon.
title: Africa: Black Rhinos Are Mostly Loners, but Not Always - Why This Matters for Saving the Species

description: [The Conversation Africa] As communities around the world shore up their infrastructure in anticipation of one of the most powerful El Niños on record in late 2026 and early 2027, they need to think about rising health risks, too - and include them in early weather warnings.
title: Africa: El Niño Threatens Health, Too - Early Warnings Done Right Can Save Lives
